rows.question: Where should an object be placed in front of a convex lens to get a real and enlarged image of the object ?
rows.opt_c: Between the principal focus and twice the focal length
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Between the principal focus and twice the focal length. A slide projector uses this setting, with the slide a little outside the focus and a big real picture on the distant screen.

rows.question: The magnetic field lines inside a current carrying long solenoid are in the form of
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.theme: Concept 1.3.1: Magnetic Fields & Magnetic Effects of Current
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: parallel straight lines. A solenoid is a long coil of insulated wire wound closely in the shape of a cylinder.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Magnetic Fields & Magnetic Effects of Current

rows.question: A ray of light travelling from a rarer medium to a denser medium
rows.opt_a: slows down and bends away from the normal.
rows.opt_b: slows down and bends towards the normal.
rows.opt_c: speeds up and bends away from the normal.
rows.opt_d: speeds up and bends towards the normal.
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: slows down and bends towards the normal. So a ray crossing from a rarer medium into a denser one loses speed at the boundary and bends towards the normal.

rows.question: An electric circuit is consisting of a cell, an ammeter and a nichrome wire of length l. If the length of the wire is reduced to half (l/2), then the ammeter reading
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: gets doubled. The ammeter is in series and reads that current, so its reading doubles.

rows.question: What is the effect of pressure of a human body on sand ?
rows.opt_a: Larger while standing than while lying
rows.opt_b: Smaller while standing than while lying
rows.opt_d: Larger while standing during the daytime and smaller during the night time while lying
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.theme: Concept 1.11.1: Buoyancy, Archimedes’ Principle & Floating Bodies
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Larger while standing than while lying. Pressure is thrust divided by the area over which the thrust acts, and thrust is the force acting perpendicular to the surface.

rows.question: An athlete completes one round of a circular track of diameter 100 m in 20 s. What will be the displacements after 1 minute and 10 s, respectively ?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: 0 m, 100 m. The straight-line distance between those two points is the diameter of the circle, 100 m.

rows.question: Which of the following statements about universal indicator is/are true ? 1. It is a mixture of several indicators. 2. It shows different colours at different concentrations of hydrogen ions in solution. 3. It helps to determine the strength of given acid and base in titration. Select the correct answer using the code given below :
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.subtopic: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
tags: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: 1, 2 and 3. Dilute hydrochloric acid and dilute ethanoic acid of the same concentration show different colours, because the first ionises far more completely.

rows.question: Which of the following carbon allotropes is/are good conductor(s) of electricity? 1. Diamond 2. Graphite 3. Fullerene Select the correct answer using the code given below:
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: 2 only. Graphite is the one allotrope on the list that conducts electricity well.

rows.question: What is the approximate percentage of carbon in the Earth's crust?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.theme: Rock Cycle, Rock Types & Mineral Properties
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: 0.025%. Carbon is everywhere in living matter and almost nowhere in the rocks.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Rock Cycle, Rock Types & Mineral Properties

rows.question: When copper reacts with moist carbon dioxide (CO₂) in air, it forms a green coating of which one of the following compounds?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.theme: Concept 2.5.1: Physical & Chemical Properties of Metals and Non-Metals
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Cupric carbonate. Copper left in damp air slowly loses its shiny brown surface and takes on a green coat.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Physical & Chemical Properties of Metals and Non-Metals

rows.question: What is the name of the process that converts sulphide ores into oxides by heating strongly in the presence of excess air?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.theme: Concept 2.5.1: Physical & Chemical Properties of Metals and Non-Metals
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Roasting. Zinc blende is the standard illustration: zinc sulphide heated in a current of air gives zinc oxide and sulphur dioxide.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Physical & Chemical Properties of Metals and Non-Metals

rows.question: What are the constituents of alloy solder?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.theme: Concept 2.5.1: Physical & Chemical Properties of Metals and Non-Metals
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Pb and Sn. That low melting point is its whole use.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Physical & Chemical Properties of Metals and Non-Metals

rows.question: Which of the following limits the number of trophic levels in a food chain?
rows.opt_c: Decrease in the available energy at higher trophic levels
rows.subject: Environment
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Decrease in the available energy at higher trophic levels. Energy also moves one way through the chain and never returns to a previous level, so what is lost cannot be recovered.

rows.question: In pea, a pure tall plant (TT) is crossed with a short plant (tt). What will be the ratio of pure tall plants to short plants in the F₂ generation?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: 1: 1. Pure tall means TT alone, since Tt plants are tall but not pure-breeding, and short means tt.

rows.question: Which one of the following statements about variations is not true?
rows.opt_a: Variation is minimum in asexual reproduction.
rows.opt_b: All variations in a species have equal chances of survival.
rows.opt_c: Changes in genetic constitution result in variation.
rows.opt_d: Variants can be selected by environmental factors.
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: All variations in a species have equal chances of survival. The other three statements are true as printed.

rows.question: While studying vegetation of an area, terms like 'population' and 'community' are often used. Which one of the following statements best describes a population?
rows.opt_a: A group of organisms of one species, living in the same area at the same time.
rows.opt_b: A group of organisms of one species living in different areas during different seasons.
rows.opt_c: A unit consisting of biotic and abiotic components.
rows.opt_d: A group of organisms of more than one species, living in the same area at the same time.
rows.subject: Environment
rows.explanation: Option A is correct. One species is the crucial restriction: the moment more than one species is involved, the correct word is community.

rows.question: In the human body, blood flows through a process of double circulation. Which one of the following statements is true in this regard?
rows.opt_a: Oxygenated blood reaches the left side of the heart from the lungs.
rows.opt_b: Blood in the left side of the heart is poor in oxygen and is brought to the right side of the heart.
rows.opt_c: Deoxygenated blood from the left side of the heart is brought to the lungs for oxygenation.
rows.opt_d: Oxygenated blood from the right side of the heart is sent around the body.
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Oxygenated blood reaches the left side of the heart from the lungs. The blood thus passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit, which is what double circulation names.

rows.question: In which of the following groups of organisms, is food material broken down outside the body and absorbed?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Yeast, mushroom, bread mould. Breaking food down outside the body and then absorbing the products is saprophytic nutrition, and it is what fungi do.

rows.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 4 kHz and wavelength 30 cm. How long will it take to travel 2·4 km?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: 2·0 s. The journey is 2·4 km, which is 2400 m, and time is distance divided by speed: 2400 ÷ 1200 = 2 s.

rows.question: An electric bulb is connected to a 110 V generator. The current is 0·2 A. What is the power of the bulb?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: 22 W. The only place to slip is the decimal in the current.

rows.question: Refraction of light, as it enters from one transparent medium to another, is due to
rows.opt_a: change in temperature of the media.
rows.opt_b: change in the amplitude of light.
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: change in speed of light. Picture the wavefront rather than the ray.

rows.question: A bus starting from a bus-stand and moving with uniform acceleration attains a speed of 20 km/h in 10 minutes. What is its acceleration?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: 120 km/h². Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time taken.

rows.question: Which one of the following is the correct reactivity order of metals reacting with dilute HCl?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.theme: Concept 2.5.1: Physical & Chemical Properties of Metals and Non-Metals
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Mg > Al > Zn > Fe. Copper, sitting below hydrogen, gives no hydrogen with dilute hydrochloric acid at all.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Physical & Chemical Properties of Metals and Non-Metals

rows.question: Which one of the following acids is secreted by leaves of Nettle that causes painful stings?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.subtopic: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
tags: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Methanoic acid. The stinging hairs of the nettle leaf inject methanoic acid, and that is what produces the burning pain.

rows.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. All the bases are alkali. 2. All alkalis dissolve in water. 3. Alkalis are soapy to touch, bitter in taste and corrosive in nature. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.subtopic: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
tags: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: 2 and 3 only. So every alkali is a base, but not every base is an alkali; copper hydroxide and iron hydroxide are bases that stay insoluble.

rows.question: Which one of the following materials is present in a guard tube (drying tube) that is used for preparation of HCl gas?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.subtopic: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
tags: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Calcium chloride. Drying matters because the experiment shows that dry hydrogen chloride gas has no acidic character (it leaves dry litmus paper unchanged).

rows.question: Fertilizers are used to obtain higher yields of crops. However, all nutrients are usually not available in fertilizers. Which one of the following nutrients is usually not available in fertilizers?
rows.subject: Economy
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Iron. Ordinary bagged fertilizer targets the macronutrients, which is why its shorthand is N-P-K.

rows.question: Rupa and Sachin observed an animal in their school garden. Rupa called it an insect while Sachin identified it as an earthworm. Which one of the following characteristics confirms that it is an insect ?
rows.opt_b: Body of the animal had very little segmentation.
rows.opt_c: Body of the animal was cylindrical.
rows.opt_d: Body of the animal was bilaterally symmetrical.
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: The animal had jointed legs. The other three characteristics are why the disagreement was possible, because insects and earthworms share every one of them.

rows.question: Animals which are marine, bilaterally symmetrical, have a coelom and a notochord, but never form a vertebral column are placed under which one of the following groups ?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Protochordata. Vertebrates are defined by a true vertebral column and an internal skeleton, so an animal that never develops one cannot be placed there.

rows.question: What is the location of intercalary meristem in plants ?
rows.opt_a: Base of the leaves or internodes
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.theme: Concept 3.4.1: Plant Tissue Systems & Structural Anatomy
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Base of the leaves or internodes. Meristematic tissue is the dividing tissue of a plant, and it is classified by position.

rows.question: The federation of which one of the following States has been described as “an indestructible union of indestructible states” ?
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: U.S.A. The phrase is a quotation from Chief Justice Salmon P.

rows.question: Who among the following is the author of the famous essay, ‘The End of History and the Last Man’ ?
rows.subject: International Relations
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Francis Fukuyama. His claim was never that events would stop happening.

rows.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct ?
rows.opt_a: Allahabad High Court has a Bench at Lucknow.
rows.opt_b: Madhya Pradesh High Court has a Bench at Gwalior.
rows.opt_c: Rajasthan High Court is located at Jodhpur.
rows.opt_d: Guwahati High Court has no Bench.
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: Guwahati High Court has no Bench. The other three statements are sound, and since only one statement can be false, the Guwahati claim is the answer.

rows.question: Which among the following is not a condition for the disqualification of a Member of Parliament ?
rows.opt_a: Voluntary acquisition of citizenship of a foreign country
rows.opt_b: Holding the office of the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women
rows.opt_c: The Member abstains from voting in the House without prior permission
rows.opt_d: The Member holds the office of the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the National Coal Development Corporation Ltd.
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Holding the office of the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women. That law is the Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959, and its section 3 lists the protected offices.

rows.question: Who among the following considered the Directive Principles of State Policy as aiming at 'furthering the goals of social exclusion'?
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Granville Austin. None of the other three names is associated with that formulation.

rows.question: D performs her train journey by the shortest route from Bengaluru to New Delhi. Which one of the following rivers will she not cross while performing the journey?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.theme: River Systems, Basins & Drainage Patterns of India
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Yamuna. Read the journey as a line drawn north from the Deccan and ask which rivers lie across it.
rows.taxonomy_concept: River Systems, Basins & Drainage Patterns of India

rows.question: Identify the State on the basis of the following characteristics: 1. Tropic of Cancer passes through the State. 2. The State has more north-south extension. 3. The State has international border with Bangladesh and Myanmar. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Mizoram. Mizoram's 722 km of international boundary is shared with Bangladesh on the west and Myanmar on the east and south; Tripura touches Myanmar nowhere.

rows.question: M wants to visit a place in a Union Territory, which is located at 34° N and 77° E. Which one of the following Union Territories must he have planned to visit?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: Ladakh. Nothing else on the list is even close.

rows.question: Consider the following statements with respect to the adolescent population (age group of 10 to 19 years) of India, according to the 2011 Census: 1. Adolescent population comprises half the population of the country. 2. The group is regarded as youthful population with high potential. 3. In this group there are greater number of females than males. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: 2 only. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: In a discussion, M from Arunachal Pradesh, J from Assam, N from Meghalaya and S from Nagaland are claiming that as per Census 2011, their State has the maximum density of population. Identify the person making the correct claim.
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: J. Meghalaya stood at 132, Nagaland at 119 and Arunachal Pradesh at 17, the lowest figure for any State in India.

rows.question: Who among the following ancient Indian kings was praised in glowing terms in the Prayaga Prashasti?
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Samudragupta. This matches the specific fact or definition tested in the question.

rows.question: The Self-Respect Movement was initiated by
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: E. V. Ramaswamy Naicker. The Self-Respect Movement began in Tamil country in 1925 and is inseparable from the man everyone calls Periyar.

rows.question: The location of the ancient city of Taxila (Takshshila), mentioned in ancient Indian texts, was identified by
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Alexander Cunnigham. Note that the booklet prints the surname as Cunnigham, a slip of a letter, and Takshshila for Takshashila.

rows.question: Who among the following was not a Jain Acharya?
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Khema. Khema belongs to the other heterodox tradition altogether.

rows.question: In India, the first major public appearance of Mahatma Gandhi was in
rows.subject: History
rows.theme: Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India & Gandhian thought
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Inauguration of Banaras Hindu University (1916). This best matches the concept described in the question.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India & Gandhian thought

rows.question: Consider the following statements about Patanjali's Mahabhashya: 1. It makes a mention of Kautilya. 2. It is a book on grammar and refers to historical personalities only incidentally. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: 2 only. Patanjali's Mahabhashya, composed in about the mid-second century BCE, is a commentary on selected rules of Panini's Ashtadhyayi together with Katyayana's varttikas on them.

rows.question: Which one of the following may lead to movement along the demand curve of a commodity?
rows.opt_b: Change in price of the other commodities
rows.opt_c: Change in income of the consumer
rows.opt_d: Change in tastes and preferences of consumers
rows.subject: Economy
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Change in its price. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: Which one of the following is the opportunity cost of a chosen activity?
rows.opt_b: Out of pocket cost plus cost incurred by the Government
rows.opt_d: Value of next best alternative that is given up
rows.subject: Economy
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: Value of next best alternative that is given up. Opportunity cost is what economics substitutes for the accountant's idea of cost.

rows.question: Which one of the following statements in the context of social sector spending in India during 2014–19 (both States and the Union Government together) is true?
rows.opt_a: Expenditure on education was 5% of GDP.
rows.opt_b: Expenditure on health was 4% of the social services expenditure.
rows.opt_c: There was a stagnation in the spending on education as a percent of GDP.
rows.opt_d: Health sector spending amounted to 10% of the total expenditure.
rows.subject: Economy
rows.explanation: Option C is correct. That is why the six per cent of GDP target first set in 1968 has stayed out of reach.

rows.question: According to UNDP's Human Development Report – 2020, in which of the HDI components has India improved in recent years? 1. Life expectancy at birth 2. Expected years of schooling 3. GNI per capita 4. Mean years of schooling Select the correct answer using the code given below :
rows.subject: Economy
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: 1 and 3 only. The Human Development Index has three dimensions and four indicators.

rows.question: Which one of the following is true of a pure voluntary exchange between two parties A and B?
rows.opt_a: A can exploit B or vice versa
rows.opt_b: Both gain; it is a win-win situation
rows.opt_c: If A makes profit, it must be at the cost of B
rows.subject: Economy
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Both gain; it is a win-win situation. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: The provision, ‘the State shall take steps to separate the Judiciary from the Executive in the public services of the State’ is incorporated in which part of the Constitution of India?
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Part-IV. The Article is usually grouped with the liberal-intellectual Directive Principles rather than the socialist or Gandhian ones.

rows.question: Which of the following statements are correct? 1. Speaker may permit any Member to address the House in his/her mother tongue, if he/she cannot adequately express in either Hindi or English. 2. Business of the Parliamentary Committees is transacted either in Hindi or in English. 3. The minutes of the Parliamentary Committees are prepared invariably in Hindi or English. Select the correct answer using the code given below :
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: 1, 2 and 3. The reason is practical: the minutes and report must be usable by the whole House, the Government and any court that later reads them.

rows.question: Which one of the following is the correct meaning of the term ‘State’, as defined in Article 12 of the Constitution of India?
rows.opt_a: It refers only to the Government of India.
rows.opt_b: It refers only to the Government of India and the Parliament of India.
rows.opt_c: It refers only to the Government of India, Parliament of India, and Governments and Legislatures of each State.
rows.opt_d: It refers to the Government of India, Parliament of India, Governments and Legislatures of each State, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India.
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option D is correct. Article 12 is a definition clause, and it is deliberately the widest of the four options.

rows.question: Which one among the following is the largest State in terms of seats in the Rajya Sabha?
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Bihar. Note the limit of the claim: Bihar is the largest of these four, not of the country.

rows.question: Under which Article of the Constitution of India has provision been made for reservation of seats for women in Panchayats?
rows.subject: Polity
rows.theme: rd Amendment, Panchayats & Rural Local Government
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Article 243 D. Article 243D is the reservation Article.

rows.question: The painted illustration of the moving of the Ashoka Pillar at Topra is found in
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Sirat-i-Firuz Shahi. The Topra shaft was moved in the 1350s and re-erected beside the Friday mosque of his new city of Firuzabad.

rows.question: Which one among the following is a temple of the Vaishnavite tradition?
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Srirangam. The other three are all Shaiva foundations of the Tamil country, which makes the item a test of tradition rather than of geography.

rows.question: The biography of Shaikh Muinuddin Chishti, authored by Jahanara, is known as
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Munis al Arwah. It is also a remarkable first-person record of a Mughal princess's pilgrimage.

rows.question: Which one of the following is not a political method of the moderates in the National Movement?
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Overthrow of alien rule. Their most damaging work was intellectual rather than agitational: Dadabhai Naoroji's drain of wealth argument turned poverty into an indictment of the colonial economy.

rows.question: Swami Dayanand Saraswati took inspiration from
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Vedas. Dayanand Saraswati rested his entire reform programme on one claim.

rows.question: The call for 'renunciation of (all) voluntary associations with the (British) Government' was given during
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Non-Cooperation Movement. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct with respect to Time Zone in India? 1. There is one standard time for the whole country. 2. Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep Islands have different Time Zones. 3. Indian Standard Time (IST) is five and half hours behind GMT. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
rows.subject: Geography
rows.theme: Earth Rotation, Revolution, Seasons & Time Zones
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: 1 only. Statement 2 fails on the same fact.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Earth Rotation, Revolution, Seasons & Time Zones

rows.question: D had recently visited Khardung La, Nubra Valley and several Buddhist monasteries. Which one of the following States / UT had she visited?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.theme: Indian Mountain Systems, Peaks, Glaciers & Passes
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: Ladakh. This best matches the concept described in the question.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Indian Mountain Systems, Peaks, Glaciers & Passes

rows.question: Which one of the following States receives rainfall from both the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch of Monsoon?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Punjab. The south-west monsoon reaches India in two arms, and Punjab is where both of them arrive.

rows.question: Inceptisols, Entisols, Vertisols and Mollisols are orders of which one of the following?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Soil. Nothing about sugarcane, coal or copper is classified in orders of this kind.

rows.question: S had witnessed contour bunding and contour ploughing while visiting one of the States in India. Identify the State from the options given below.
rows.subject: Geography
rows.theme: Soil Types, Distribution & Properties in India
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Himachal Pradesh. This best matches the concept described in the question.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Soil Types, Distribution & Properties in India

rows.question: Which one of the following target groups is the beneficiary of 'Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan' scheme?
rows.subject: Economy
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: All returning migrants. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists : List I (Curve) A. Lorenz curve B. Phillips curve C. Engel curve D. Laffer curve List II (Indication) 1. Inflation and employment 2. Tax rates and tax revenue 3. Inequality in distribution of income or wealth 4. Income and proportion of expenditure on food Code :
rows.subject: Economy
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: 3 1 4 2. The Phillips curve plots the rate of wage or price inflation against unemployment and traces the short-run trade-off between them: indication 1.

rows.question: Which one of the following is a typical example of monopolistic competition?
rows.subject: Economy
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Market for soaps. Monopolistic competition has three defining marks: many sellers, a product that each seller differentiates from the others, and free entry and exit.

rows.question: Following the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, the Parliament of India enacted quite a few GST Acts in the year 2017. Which one of the following does not fall in this category?
rows.opt_a: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act
rows.opt_b: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act
rows.opt_c: The Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Acts
rows.opt_d: The State Goods and Services Tax Act
rows.subject: Polity
rows.theme: Legal institutions, sources of law and major enactments
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: The State Goods and Services Tax Act. That is the one Parliament did not enact.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Legal institutions, sources of law and major enactments

rows.question: Which one of the following is not correct in respect of Directorate of Enforcement?
rows.opt_a: It is a specialized financial investigation agency under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
rows.opt_b: It enforces the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
rows.opt_c: It enforces the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
rows.opt_d: It enforces the Prohibition of Benami Property Transaction Act, 1988.
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: It enforces the Prohibition of Benami Property Transaction Act, 1988. That is the statement that does not hold.

rows.question: Which one of the following is not correct?
rows.opt_a: Taxes on agricultural income is a subject under the State List.
rows.opt_b: Price control is a subject under the Concurrent List.
rows.opt_c: Insurance does not come under the Union List.
rows.opt_d: 'Forests' is a subject under the Concurrent List.
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Insurance does not come under the Union List. This is the exception; the remaining choices satisfy the condition stated in the question.

rows.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct about the nature of India's federal system?
rows.opt_a: There is no equality of representation of States in the Council of States.
rows.opt_b: Sikkim was not initially included in the Union as a full-fledged State.
rows.opt_c: Special provisions have been laid down in the Constitution of India for Andhra Pradesh under Article 371 D.
rows.opt_d: The Constitution of India enables the federal government to acquire the strength of a unitary system during emergencies.
rows.subject: Polity
rows.drop_reason: Dropped by product decision: source marks question cancelled.

rows.question: The Constitution of India guarantees freedom of speech and expression. But the freedom is subject to certain reasonable restrictions imposed by the State. These restrictions may relate to which of the following? 1. Defamation 2. Decency or morality 3. Incitement to an offence Select the correct answer using the code given below:
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: 1, 2 and 3. Decency or morality appears there in those exact words, and defamation and incitement to an offence close the list.

rows.question: Which one of the following amendments in the Constitution of India made a Proclamation of Emergency immune from judicial review?
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: 42nd Amendment. It also inserted Articles 32A, 131A, 144A, 226A and 228A.

rows.question: Which one of the following British officials was elevated to the position of Governor General after the Regulating Act of 1773?
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Warren Hastings. Warren Hastings held the Bengal governorship at the time and so became the first holder of the new office, serving until 1785.

rows.question: Which of the following ideas was preached by the Kherwar or Sapha Har movement of the 1870s?
rows.opt_a: Acceptance of the Hindu pantheonic order
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Monotheism and internal social reform. Its two names carry its programme.

rows.question: In which one of the following years was the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha established?
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: 1870. This matches the specific fact or definition tested in the question.

rows.question: Which one of the following was an important Pandya port, celebrated for its pearls in Sangam poems and Greek accounts?
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Korkai. Silt has since pushed the coastline several kilometres away, so the site now lies inland.

rows.question: The town of Chisht, from which the Sufi Chishti Silsila derives its name, is located in
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Central Afghanistan. The Chishtis are of the second kind.

rows.question: The rules for congregational worship (Sangat) involving collective recitation were organized by
rows.subject: History
rows.theme: Ahom, Kashmir, Odisha, Assam and other regional traditions
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Guru Nanak. He also appointed his disciple Angad to succeed him as guru, and the succession ran for nearly two centuries.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Ahom, Kashmir, Odisha, Assam and other regional traditions

rows.question: Who amongst the following will be at more risk with respect to the earthquake hazard zone specified by the Geological Survey of India?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Malti at Pithoragarh. Uttarakhand government disaster-management material places the district in Zone V, the highest category on the Indian zoning map.

rows.question: The Government wants to prepare a plan for drought prone areas of the country. Which one of the following regions will be predominantly focused?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: Kutch region. None of the other three regions is arid.

rows.question: Four persons are travelling to different States of India. To whom will you advise to protect oneself from blizzards?
rows.opt_a: The person travelling to Arunachal Pradesh
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: The person travelling to Arunachal Pradesh. That combination requires high, cold, snow-covered country, and of the four States named only Arunachal Pradesh has it.

rows.question: Which one of the following States is not prominent for plantation agriculture?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Rajasthan. Every one of those crops needs plentiful and dependable water, and most need warm humid conditions and often a slope with good drainage.

rows.question: The distance between which two cities has been reduced by the Atal Tunnel?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Manali to Leh. That year-round access to the first leg of the Manali-Leh road is why the tunnel matters strategically as well as commercially.

rows.question: Which one of the following biosphere reserves comprises islands with estuaries, beaches, coral reefs, salt marshes and mangroves?
rows.subject: Environment
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Gulf of Mannar biosphere reserve. It is also the flagship habitat of the dugong in Indian waters.

rows.question: Which one of the following is not a correct statement with reference to the Constitution of India?
rows.opt_a: The Constitution (Eighty-Fifth) Amendment Act has inserted the 'Right to Education' under Article 21A.
rows.opt_c: Right to Constitutional Remedies is in Part-III of the Constitution.
rows.opt_d: Writ jurisdiction of High Courts is wider than the Supreme Court of India.
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option A is correct. This is the exception; the remaining choices satisfy the condition stated in the question.

rows.question: Which one of the following statements about the Cripps Mission is not correct?
rows.opt_a: It was sent to India by the British Government in March 1942.
rows.opt_b: It proposed that the Constitution of India was to be framed by an elected Constituent Assembly of the Indian people.
rows.opt_c: Any province which was not prepared to accept the Constitution would be free to retain its constitutional provisions existing at that time.
rows.opt_d: The British Government could enter into a separate constitutional arrangement with any of the acceding provinces.
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option D is correct. The other three statements are accurate as printed.

rows.question: Which of the following statements regarding constitutional amendment is/are correct? 1. The procedure for amendment to the Constitution is provided in Article 368. 2. A Bill to amend the Constitution can be introduced in either House of the Parliament. 3. The special procedure in Article 368 vests constituent powers upon the ordinary legislation. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: 1, 2 and 3. Statement 3 is where candidates stall.

rows.question: Which one of the following is not a circumstance for proclamation of Emergency by the President of India under Article 352 of the Constitution of India?
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Internal disturbance. This is the exception; the remaining choices satisfy the condition stated in the question.

rows.question: Akbar issued a Farman in 1598 permitting in the city of Cambay (Khambat), Gujarat, the construction of a
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Church. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: Domingo Paes, the medieval traveller, has described the city of
rows.subject: History
rows.theme: Ahom, Kashmir, Odisha, Assam and other regional traditions
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Vijayanagara. He also described the huge tank Krishnadeva Raya built, fed by water brought from more than three leagues away through pipes.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Ahom, Kashmir, Odisha, Assam and other regional traditions

rows.question: The extent of damage caused by earthquake is not influenced by which one of the following?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: Climate of the area. Population density covers the second, which is why casualty figures track settlement and not magnitude alone.

rows.question: An avalanche is a type of which one of the following disasters?
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Terrestrial. The sorting rule is where the event happens, not what set it off.

rows.question: An infection constantly maintained at a baseline level in a geographic area without external input is known as
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Endemic. The other three options all describe departures from the steady state rather than the steady state itself.

rows.question: Streams and rivers coming from the mountains deposit heavy materials of rocks and boulders in
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Bhabar. The belt is so coarse and permeable that the smaller streams sink into it and vanish underground, to re-emerge a little further south.

rows.question: Which of the following statements regarding the electoral rolls is/are correct? 1. There is one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency. 2. No person is ineligible for inclusion in the electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or any of them. 3. A citizen of India, not less than 18 years of age, can cast his/her vote unless disqualified under a law of an appropriate legislature. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: 1, 2 and 3. All three statements are drawn from two short articles of the Constitution.

rows.question: Which one of the following statements is not correct about ‘Totalitarianism’?
rows.opt_a: It is not akin to autocracy and authoritarianism.
rows.opt_b: It usurps political freedom of the individuals, but it doesn’t usurp personal freedoms.
rows.opt_c: It implies abolition of civil society.
rows.opt_d: It is usually identified with a one-party state.
rows.subject: Polity
rows.theme: Democracy, Liberty, Equality, Socialism & Political Ideologies
rows.explanation: Option B is correct. That statement fails on the point that defines the term.
rows.taxonomy_concept: Democracy, Liberty, Equality, Socialism & Political Ideologies

rows.question: Who among the following was chosen for the Kuvempu Award 2020?
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Dr. Rajendra Kishore Panda. He published some sixteen collections of verse along with fiction, including the novel Chidabhas, and he died in 2025.

rows.question: Avani Lekhara became the first Indian woman to win two Paralympics medals at the Tokyo Paralympics 2020. Which one of the following was her discipline?
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Shooting. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: Bagram Air Base is located in
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Afghanistan. Bagram Airfield lies in Parwan province, about eleven kilometres south-east of Charikar and some forty kilometres from Kabul.

rows.question: The Panchmuli Lake is situated near
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: Statue of Unity. Panchmuli Lake lies inside the Statue of Unity tourism complex at Kevadia, now renamed Ekta Nagar, in Narmada district of Gujarat.

rows.question: Pinaka, developed in India, is a
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.subtopic: Missile Systems, Ballistic Trajectories & ASAT Tech
rows.theme: Concept 5.1.1: Missile Systems & Ballistic Missile Technology
tags: Missile Systems, Ballistic Trajectories & ASAT Tech
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: multi-barrel rocket launcher. The name is taken from the bow of Shiva.

rows.question: What is itat e-dwar?
rows.opt_a: An Urdu magazine published from Lucknow
rows.opt_b: An e-filing portal of Income Tax Appellate Tribunal
rows.opt_d: Name of a UNESCO world heritage site
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: An e-filing portal of Income Tax Appellate Tribunal. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: What is the range capability of Agni-P Ballistic Missile?
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.subtopic: Missile Systems, Ballistic Trajectories & ASAT Tech
rows.theme: Concept 5.1.1: Missile Systems & Ballistic Missile Technology
tags: Missile Systems, Ballistic Trajectories & ASAT Tech
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: 1,000 – 2,000 km. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: Which one of the following Indian States has recently declared itself as the first rabies-free State?
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: Goa. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: Department of Public Enterprises is a part of
rows.subject: Polity
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Ministry of Finance. The Ministry of Heavy Industries kept the administration of the engineering and automobile sector and the public enterprises that belong to it.

rows.question: Chronologically arrange the following Indian-origin astronauts on the basis of their flying into space starting with the first: 1. Sunita Williams 2. Rakesh Sharma 3. Sirisha Bandla 4. Kalpana Chawla Select the correct answer using the code given below:
rows.subject: Science & Technology
rows.subtopic: Space Engineering, Satellite Orbits & Launch Systems
rows.theme: Concept 4.2.3: Astronomical Observatories & Deep Space Telescopes
tags: Space Engineering, Satellite Orbits & Launch Systems
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: 2-4-1-3. So the sequence runs Rakesh Sharma, Kalpana Chawla, Sunita Williams, Sirisha Bandla: statement 2, then 4, then 1, then 3.

rows.question: President Jovenel Moise, who was assassinated recently, was the President of which one of the following countries?
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Haiti. The killing left Haiti without a functioning presidency and deepened a political crisis that has continued since.

rows.question: Recently, which one among the following Ministries was formed under the Government of India?
rows.opt_a: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
rows.opt_b: Ministry of Development of North-Eastern Region
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Ministry of Cooperation. Being four months old when this paper was written, it was the obvious answer.

rows.question: Indian Naval Ship INS Tabar had recently participated in a two-day naval exercise with the Italian Navy. The exercise was conducted in
rows.subject: Security
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Tyrrhenian Sea. This best matches the concept described in the question.

rows.question: Which one of the following countries has recently been awarded a malaria-free certification by the WHO?
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: China. Certification is not awarded for low numbers.

rows.question: Who amongst the following was honoured with Gandhi Peace Prize for the year 2020?
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. The citation followed the terms of the award, which honours contributions towards social, economic and political transformation through non-violent and other Gandhian methods.

rows.question: Why was Dholavira in the news recently?
rows.opt_c: For the discovery of gold and precious stones at this site
rows.opt_d: It received the UNESCO World Heritage Tag
rows.subject: History
rows.explanation: Option D is correct: It received the UNESCO World Heritage Tag. What makes it exceptional, and what the inscription rests on, is water.

rows.question: Which one of the following is the oldest football tournament of Asia?
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option C is correct: Durand Cup. The Durand Cup was started in 1888 and is the oldest existing club football tournament in Asia.

rows.question: Who among the following is the first Indian woman to win a medal in the Olympics?
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Karnam Malleswari. This matches the specific fact or definition tested in the question.

rows.question: The Russian Federation participated in the Tokyo Olympics, 2020 under which of the following names?
rows.subject: Current Affairs
rows.explanation: Option A is correct: Russian Olympic Committee. Competing in that form, the ROC finished fifth on the table with twenty gold, twenty-eight silver and twenty-three bronze: seventy-one medals in all.

rows.question: Which of the following States/Union Territory/Region are in special focus in the National Mission on Edible Oils—Oil Palm?
rows.opt_a: Himachal Pradesh and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
rows.opt_b: North-East Region and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
rows.subject: Geography
rows.explanation: Option B is correct: North-East Region and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The special focus written into the scheme is on the north-eastern region and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
